prompt:
Normalize the one contact record in the user's note. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or JSON null.

Use only the record's label–value lines, not surrounding notes or signatures. Labels may vary, separator may be colon, equals or tab, and lines may be shuffled. Trim and collapse runs of whitespace in each value. Absent, blank, and whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD, any case) yield null. Do not guess or fill values from domains or company suffixes. The only missing-value exception is country from a uniquely identifying international calling code.

Country normally comes from its own line. Reassign other values by content before normalization: a value containing @ is email; a value containing at least seven digits and only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after stripping leading tel: and a trailing extension is phone. Extension forms are ext. N, ext N, xN, #N, and extension N, where N is digits. If the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not, swap the two values before cleanup.

Legal suffixes, matched case-insensitively at the end: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Remove the company's trailing suffix with its optional preceding comma and trim. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated company word. For name, split Last, First at the first comma and reverse the parts. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof with or without a dot, ignoring case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated name part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. For email, remove surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix, then lowercase the entire address.

Normalize a provided country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes in any case, and common aliases (UK / Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA / U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ).

After dropping tel: and any extension, treat a phone as international if it starts with + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. Remove literal (0) on this branch before stripping spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Convert leading 00 to + and keep the written calling code. A provided country stays as given after normalization even if the phone code disagrees. If country is absent, blank or a placeholder, infer it from the international calling code only if unique; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For a national phone, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk zero if present and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code. With no country, a national phone is null. Phone strings use E.164: + followed only by digits.

Worked example — input:
Please archive this after the handover.
Name = VEXQUILL MERE, B.V.
Org: ŽERNUVIK, Mx. LÚMI-TÉVA
E-mail: tel:(+31) (0)26/583.74.92 x63
Tel = <mailto:LT.ZERNUVIK@VEXQUILL-MERE.invalid>
Land: tBd

Output:
{"name":"Lúmi-Téva Žernuvik","phone":"+31265837492","email":"lt.zernuvik@vexquill-mere.invalid","company":"Vexquill Mere","country":"NL"}
